title: LangChain adds AI Search to LangSmith for debugging AI agents
key_facts: LangChain has added AI Search to LangSmith, letting developers search AI agent traces by describing a behaviour in plain language.
It is meant to find cases such as an agent wrongly claiming a task is complete, an unwanted response or exposed personal data.
A decision model examines trace content rather than relying on text similarity; natural-language queries can be combined with existing filters.

SmithDB, LangChain's database for agent observability, converts traces into standardised trajectories; it supports traces from LangChain, LangGraph, OpenAI, Anthropic, Vercel AI SDK and OpenTelemetry.
Each trajectory gets an 8,000-token budget, so the decision model does not see every detail of long sessions.
In 150 sampled conversations from LangChain's coding agent Open SWE, the median had about 72,000 tokens and tool outputs made up about 85%.
LangChain says it is looking at query-dependent context selection and extra checks.
quote_evidence: AI Search examines recorded agent interactions and returns traces that match a developer’s query.
AI Search addresses these large records by applying an 8,000-token budget to each trajectory before passing it to the decision model.
LangChain acknowledged that detecting behaviours such as an agent ignoring a tool error requires access to the corresponding tool result.
why_it_matters_hint: Developers can find agent failures that raise no error by describing the behaviour, with a stated limit on long sessions.
notes: Developer Tech relays LangChain's announcement; limits are LangChain's own admission.
